_note: Geometry for the schematic map of the project. Tunnel routes are drawn smoothly from point to point: no alignment has been studied. Corridor lengths are planning estimates read from maps; the four approach corridors end where the tunnels come up on the existing tracks, at the ring road (east: at Rosa Parks, just inside it); line H comes up near Pont-Cardinet; the link is 5 km (4.5 to 6). Each corridor lists the tunnels that run in it (tgv, ter, n, h), as model.tunnels.corridors. The Seine and the existing lines are sketched by hand for orientation.

stations.name: Paris Nord-Est
stations.where: Under and between Gare du Nord and Gare de l’Est, which are 500 m apart.
stations.calls: TGVs of all four lines stop here, from the north, the east, the south-east and the Atlantic; one of the six TGV tracks can be closed off for each London departure. Regional express trains from the north and the east run through to Montparnasse, line N from the east runs through to Montparnasse, and line H from the north runs on to Saint-Lazare.
stations.surface: Every train of Gare du Nord and Gare de l’Est goes underground, so all the surface tracks of both stations are freed: both halls become entrances, and the platforms and approach tracks become one park.
stations.under: under Gare du Nord and Gare de l’Est
stations.stage_note: TGV and line H platforms in stage 1; regional express and line N platforms in stage 2.

stations.name: Gare de Lyon
stations.calls: TGVs only: those of the south-east, and the half of the northern, eastern and Atlantic TGVs that pair with them. A junction at the city end leads to the direct link to Montparnasse.
stations.surface: The hall is kept as the entrance. The TGVs go underground, but the regional express trains, line R and the Bercy trains stay on the surface tracks for now (open item: Gare de Lyon regional trains), so only part of the tracks towards Bercy can become a park, and later.

stations.name: Montparnasse
stations.calls: TGVs of the Atlantic, and the half of the northern, eastern and south-eastern TGVs that pair with them; regional express trains running through from the north and the east and on to the Chartres, Le Mans and Granville lines; line N running through to Nord-Est. A junction at the city end leads to the direct link to Gare de Lyon.
stations.surface: Every train goes underground. The hall is kept as the entrance; the surface tracks towards the ring road become a park.

stations.name: Saint-Lazare
stations.where: Deep under the present station, a new through station for line H only.
stations.calls: Line H only: trains from the north (formerly lines H and K) run through Nord-Est to here, then back up onto the Batignolles tracks at Pont-Cardinet and on to the branches of line L, which become further branches of line H. The point is less Saint-Lazare itself, which RER E already serves, than a ride without a change from the northern suburbs to Pont-Cardinet, Clichy-Levallois, Courbevoie and La Défense.
stations.surface: The surface station stays as it is, for line J and the Normandy trains: no park here, and no new hall.

junctions.name: Northern junction
junctions.what: Where the TGV tunnels from the north and from the east become one, and the regional express tunnels too, just before the station. Line H comes from the north only and line N from the east only, so they need no junction.

junctions.name: Southern junction
junctions.what: Where the TGV tunnels to Gare de Lyon and to Montparnasse part, just after the station. The regional express and line N tunnels run on to Montparnasse only, and line H turns west to Saint-Lazare, so they need no junction.

junctions.name: Montparnasse junction
junctions.what: Where the direct link to Gare de Lyon leaves the TGV tunnel from Nord-Est, at the city end of Montparnasse. Its geometry has not been designed.

junctions.name: Gare de Lyon junction
junctions.what: Where the direct link from Montparnasse joins the TGV tunnel from Nord-Est, at the city end of Gare de Lyon. Its geometry has not been designed.
